findings.highlight: She leans forward expectantly.
findings.evidenceJa: ずい、と身を乗り出して問いただしてくる
findings.governingReading: she thrusts herself forward and presses him for an answer
findings.explanation: Saber’s forceful demand for a decision becomes passive expectation.

findings.highlight: We should be going out in search of other Masters
findings.evidenceJa: 犠牲者を出さない為にも、他のマスターを捜すぐらいはするべき
findings.governingReading: to prevent any more victims, we should at least search for the other Masters
findings.explanation: Shirou’s protective reason and the limited scope of his proposed action disappear.

findings.highlight: Damn.
findings.evidenceJa: まいったな
findings.governingReading: This is a problem
findings.explanation: Shirou’s troubled uncertainty is given a harsher expletive.

findings.highlight: I’ve met her once before
findings.evidenceJa: 前にすれ違った事もある
findings.governingReading: we crossed paths once before
findings.explanation: A brief passing encounter is promoted into a meeting.

findings.highlight: Saber gives me a hard look.
findings.evidenceJa: 難しそうな顔でこっちを見据えてきた
findings.governingReading: Saber fixes him with a troubled, grave expression
findings.explanation: Saber’s concern and deliberation become a hostile or stern look.

findings.highlight: how the Einzbern girl was doing
findings.evidenceJa: アインツベルンの娘は健在か
findings.governingReading: whether the Einzbern girl was still alive and well
findings.explanation: The earlier speaker’s question about survival becomes a casual inquiry after well-being.

findings.highlight: You should go to the church
findings.evidenceJa: もう一度教会に赴くべき
findings.governingReading: you should go to the church once more
findings.explanation: The fact that Saber knowingly sends Shirou back to a place already visited disappears.

findings.highlight: answer your questions and guide you to the path you must take
findings.evidenceJa: 疑問にも、これから取るべき道にも示唆を与えてくれる
findings.governingReading: give you indications concerning both your questions and the path you should take
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s provision of suggestive clues becomes direct answers and authoritative guidance.

findings.highlight: unless I want to revoke my Command Spell
findings.evidenceJa: マスターを放棄する時以外は来るな
findings.governingReading: do not return unless he intends to relinquish being a Master
findings.explanation: A rule about abandoning Master status is changed into revoking one Command Spell.

findings.highlight: That rule is only part of the face he puts up for his association.
findings.evidenceJa: あの神父が敷いているルールは魔術師同士の戦いを律する為に作られた、協会側の建前
findings.governingReading: the priest’s rules are the Association’s public pretext, created to regulate conflict among magi
findings.explanation: An institutional rule system is mistranslated as a personal facade Kotomine maintains for an unnamed association.

findings.highlight: It has no power if you are not part of their association.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術協会に属しているのなら従う価値もありますが
findings.governingReading: if Shirou belonged to the Mage’s Association, the rules would be worth obeying
findings.explanation: The positive side of Saber’s conditional rule hierarchy disappears.

findings.highlight: It has no power if you are not part of their association.
findings.evidenceJa: 所属していないのならば何の価値もありません
findings.governingReading: if he does not belong, those rules have no value for him
findings.explanation: A judgment about practical obligation becomes a claim that the rules lack power.

findings.highlight: we don’t
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮の家は協会に属さないアウトローだ
findings.governingReading: the Emiya household consists of outlaws outside the Association
findings.explanation: Shirou’s explicit family position outside institutional Magecraft disappears.

findings.highlight: we can ignore them
findings.evidenceJa: 切嗣同様無視してもかまわない
findings.governingReading: he may ignore the rules just as Kiritsugu did
findings.explanation: The inherited precedent connecting Shirou’s decision to Kiritsugu disappears.

findings.highlight: but are under no obligation
findings.evidenceJa: 従う義務はない
findings.governingReading: but you are under no obligation
findings.explanation: The English sentence lacks its subject.

findings.highlight: It’s not that I feel enmity or danger.
findings.evidenceJa: 危険だとか信用できないとか、そういう敵対意識からじゃない
findings.governingReading: this is not hostility arising from thinking him dangerous or untrustworthy
findings.explanation: Shirou distinguishes his fear from both danger and distrust; the latter disappears.

findings.highlight: I might crumble in front of him
findings.evidenceJa: 会えば会うほど今まで築き上げてきた自分が崩れてしまいそう
findings.governingReading: the more he meets Kotomine, the more the self he has built until now seems likely to collapse
findings.explanation: A cumulative threat to Shirou’s constructed identity becomes momentary loss of composure in Kotomine’s presence.

findings.highlight: She declares this with a straight face.
findings.evidenceJa: 凛とした瞳のまま断言するセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber states it firmly without losing the dignity in her eyes
findings.explanation: Saber’s resolute bearing becomes the idiom for speaking seriously or without humor.

findings.highlight: I know I don’t like him, but why don’t you?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はともかく、どうしてセイバーまで苦手なんだ
findings.governingReading: leaving me aside, why are even you uncomfortable with him?
findings.explanation: Shirou’s comparison between human and Heroic Spirit becomes a casual statement that both dislike Kotomine.

findings.highlight: she lifts up her face as if to shake off her hesitation
findings.evidenceJa: 迷いを断つようにキッパリと視線をあげた
findings.governingReading: she raises her gaze decisively, as though cutting away hesitation
findings.explanation: A controlled decision expressed through Saber’s gaze is generalized to lifting her face.

findings.highlight: He cooperated all the way through to the final fight.
findings.evidenceJa: 私は彼と協力して聖杯戦争に挑み、最後まで勝ち残りました
findings.governingReading: I joined forces with him in the Holy Grail War and survived to the very end
findings.explanation: Saber’s first-person role and survival disappear, while cooperation is reassigned to Kiritsugu.

findings.highlight: He’s part of the cause of that disaster
findings.evidenceJa: あの地獄を巻き起こした一人でも、あった
findings.governingReading: he was also one of those who brought about that hell
findings.explanation: Shirou’s horrifying inference is weakened from causing hell to partial responsibility for a generic disaster.

findings.highlight: and He’s part
findings.evidenceJa: そしてあの地獄を
findings.governingReading: and he was one of
findings.explanation: Improper capitalization interrupts Shirou’s shocked thought.

findings.highlight: if you inquire him about it
findings.evidenceJa: シロウ自身が問うのならば
findings.governingReading: if you ask him yourself
findings.explanation: The verb takes the wrong object construction.

findings.highlight: I don’t feel like going in there to ask the priest about what happened ten years ago
findings.evidenceJa: あの扉を押し開け、神父に十年前の出来事を尋ねる気概が生まれない
findings.governingReading: he cannot summon the resolve to push open that door and ask about the events ten years ago
findings.explanation: A failure of courage before a concrete threshold becomes casual lack of inclination.

findings.highlight: I see a man sitting in a chair.
findings.evidenceJa: 椅子には一つだけ人影があった
findings.governingReading: there is a single figure seated there
findings.explanation: The narration identifies the stranger as male before the Japanese does.

findings.highlight: He is walking towards me in a casual manner.
findings.evidenceJa: 男はごく普通に、何をするでもなく近づいてくる
findings.governingReading: the man approaches in a perfectly ordinary way, doing nothing else
findings.explanation: Objective normality becomes a claim about the stranger’s casual attitude.

findings.highlight: That’s all he’s doing, sowhy
findings.evidenceJa: それだけだというのに、何故
findings.governingReading: That is all he is doing, so why
findings.explanation: Missing spacing fuses the causal transition.

findings.highlight: getting ready to be killed by this man
findings.evidenceJa: ここで殺されると覚悟した
findings.governingReading: became resigned to being killed here by this man
findings.explanation: An involuntary certainty and acceptance of death becomes active preparation.

findings.highlight: …Stops midair.
findings.evidenceJa: ぴたりと、空中で止まっていた
findings.governingReading: stops dead in midair
findings.explanation: Improper capitalization fragments the sentence.

findings.highlight: entranced by something unpleasant
findings.evidenceJa: よくないモノに魅入られている
findings.governingReading: captivated or possessed by something malign
findings.explanation: The stranger’s occult diagnosis is weakened into ordinary unpleasantness.

findings.highlight: I wouldn’t come here for any other reason.
findings.evidenceJa: 頼まれたっておまえの所になんて来るもんか
findings.governingReading: even if begged, he would never come to Kotomine’s place
findings.explanation: Shirou’s pointed contempt for Kotomine disappears.

findings.highlight: a good characteristic for priests
findings.evidenceJa: 神父として十分な資質
findings.governingReading: ample qualification to be a priest
findings.explanation: A judgment of Kotomine’s vocational fitness becomes a vague favorable trait.

findings.highlight: their greatest fault
findings.evidenceJa: 神父として致命的な欠陥
findings.governingReading: a fatal defect in a priest
findings.explanation: A potentially disqualifying contradiction is softened and generalized from Kotomine to priests collectively.

findings.highlight: He smiles. He does not look guilty.
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツに悪びれた様子はない
findings.governingReading: he shows no sign of guilt
findings.explanation: mirror moon invents a smile during Kotomine’s response.

findings.highlight: His disinterested tone shows no opening for a rebuttal. Kotomine’s answer isn’t wrong.
findings.evidenceJa: 言峰の返答は間違っていない
findings.governingReading: Kotomine’s answer is not wrong
findings.explanation: The English invents a disinterested tone and claims rebuttal is impossible before preserving the source statement.

findings.highlight: I studied magic as his apprentice
findings.evidenceJa: 弟子として魔術を鍛えてきた
findings.governingReading: he trained in Magecraft as Kiritsugu’s apprentice
findings.explanation: A technical discipline is called magic.

findings.highlight: I would’ve chosen to fight then and there
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はアンタの思い通り戦うと決めた筈だ
findings.governingReading: I would have decided to fight exactly as you wanted
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s potential manipulation of Shirou’s decision disappears, while unsupported immediate timing is added.

findings.highlight: an unprepared person
findings.evidenceJa: 何の用意もなく、何の覚悟もなかった人間
findings.governingReading: a person with neither preparation nor resolve
findings.explanation: The distinction between practical preparation and psychological commitment disappears.

findings.highlight: He saved me out of pure good will
findings.evidenceJa: 死のうとしていた子供を助けただけだった
findings.governingReading: he simply saved a child who was about to die, out of pure goodwill
findings.explanation: The dying child and the completed account of Kiritsugu’s rescue disappear.

findings.highlight: Emiya Kiritsugu’s sin of denying its power
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を否定した衛宮切嗣
findings.governingReading: Emiya Kiritsugu, who rejected the Grail
findings.explanation: Rejecting the Grail itself becomes denial of its power.

findings.highlight: want you to atone for Emiya Kiritsugu’s sin
findings.evidenceJa: 息子に贖罪を求めている
findings.governingReading: may be demanding atonement from Kiritsugu’s son
findings.explanation: mirror moon explicitly declares Kiritsugu’s act a sin rather than preserving Kotomine’s speculative personification of the Grail.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail thought he would be a fit owner
findings.evidenceJa: あの男にならば自らを渡してもよい、と想った
findings.governingReading: the Grail may have thought it could entrust itself to that man
findings.explanation: The Grail’s imagined willingness becomes an evaluative claim that Kiritsugu is a fit owner.

findings.highlight: But he wasn’t mistaken. But he was correct.
findings.evidenceJa: けど、それは正しいことだ
findings.governingReading: But what he did was right
findings.explanation: One source judgment is duplicated into two clashing English sentences.

findings.highlight: superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方
findings.governingReading: ally of justice
findings.explanation: Shirou’s defining ideal is replaced with a modern genre label.

findings.highlight: the Holy Grail to make his wish come true
findings.evidenceJa: “願望機”である聖杯
findings.governingReading: the Grail as a wish-granting machine
findings.explanation: A technical and thematic characterization of the Grail disappears.

findings.highlight: deemed him worthy
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツの適合性に目をつけた
findings.governingReading: noticed Kiritsugu’s compatibility
findings.explanation: Practical suitability for the Grail War becomes moral or status-based worthiness.

findings.highlight: the Einzbernsthe family of magi
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師の血族
findings.governingReading: the Einzberns—the bloodline of magi
findings.explanation: The bloodline relation disappears and two words are fused.

findings.highlight: He was named the greatest Master
findings.evidenceJa: 最高のマスターとして迎えられた
findings.governingReading: he was welcomed as an exceptional combat Master
findings.explanation: Recruitment into a role becomes the conferral of a superlative title.

findings.highlight: Kiritsugu, a strong magus who did not belong to the Magic Association
findings.evidenceJa: 殺し合いに長け、魔術協会に属さなかった切嗣
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu, who excelled at killing and stood outside the Mage’s Association
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s relevant qualification as a professional killer becomes generic magical strength.

findings.highlight: The magic of the Einzbern family is not suited for battle. Therefore
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らは戦いには不向きな一族だ
findings.governingReading: their Magecraft is unsuited to battle, and they are a bloodline unsuited to fighting
findings.explanation: The distinction between their Magecraft and the family itself disappears.

findings.highlight: gave him a woman
findings.evidenceJa: アインツベルンの血と交わる事で
findings.governingReading: by joining his blood with the Einzbern line
findings.explanation: A dynastic blood union is reduced to an unnamed woman being handed to Kiritsugu.

findings.highlight: a commoner
findings.evidenceJa: 何処の出とも判らない馬の骨
findings.governingReading: a nobody of unknown origin
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s contempt for Kiritsugu’s unknown provenance becomes a simple class distinction.

findings.highlight: brutal
findings.evidenceJa: 蛮勇
findings.governingReading: recklessly brave
findings.explanation: A paradoxical tactical trait becomes generic cruelty already expressed elsewhere in the sentence.

findings.highlight: He killed a Servant, let the Master beg for help while crawling on the floor, and ruthlessly shot him in the head.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを屠り、助けを請うマスターを這わせ、逃げようとする頭蓋に銃口を当てて
findings.governingReading: he slaughtered Servants, made pleading Masters crawl, and put a gun to the skull of one trying to flee
findings.explanation: A catalogue of Kiritsugu’s treatment of different opponents is collapsed into one Master who begs and is then shot.

findings.highlight: Neither the supremacy of his strength nor guilt in killing the weak.
findings.evidenceJa: 強さを誇る優越も、消えた弱者への罪悪もない
findings.governingReading: neither prideful superiority in his strength nor guilt toward the weak he erased
findings.explanation: The English is a sentence fragment and changes felt superiority into the supremacy of strength itself.

findings.highlight: Whatmy father was a machine
findings.evidenceJa: な切嗣が、機械
findings.governingReading: What—Kiritsugu was a machine?
findings.explanation: Missing punctuation fuses the exclamation.

findings.highlight: not involving innocent people
findings.evidenceJa: 無関係な人間を巻き込まない
findings.governingReading: not involving unrelated bystanders
findings.explanation: Noninvolvement in the conflict becomes moral innocence.

findings.highlight: the greatest evil of all
findings.evidenceJa: 前回の戦いで最も判りやすい悪
findings.governingReading: the clearest, most readily recognizable evil in the previous war
findings.explanation: A scoped comparison about recognizable evil becomes an absolute superlative.

findings.highlight: He threw away his personal feelings
findings.evidenceJa: 目的の為に私情を切り捨てた
findings.governingReading: he discarded private sentiment for the sake of his objective
findings.explanation: The English can imply removal of emotional capacity rather than rejection of personal considerations.

findings.highlight: would not obtain the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯に届かない、届く価値がない
findings.governingReading: could not reach the Grail and would not deserve to reach it
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s belief that an artificially cold persona would be unworthy disappears.

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail appeared after five Masters were defeated. It was a wish that no human could make come true
findings.evidenceJa: 所有者の前に現れた聖杯。衛宮切嗣自身が望んでいた、人の手では絶対に叶わない願い
findings.governingReading: the Grail that appeared before its owner after five Masters fell; Kiritsugu’s own impossible wish
findings.explanation: The Grail and Kiritsugu’s wish are fused by an antecedent that makes the Grail itself “a wish.”

findings.highlight: He went so far, butthat same weakness
findings.evidenceJa: そこまでして結局その弱さ
findings.governingReading: he went that far, yet in the end that weakness
findings.explanation: Missing spacing fuses the contrast.

findings.highlight: the last Holy Grail Warthe true nature
findings.evidenceJa: 前回の戦いの結末おまえが父と記憶している
findings.governingReading: the last Holy Grail War—the true nature
findings.explanation: Missing punctuation fuses two clauses.

findings.highlight: I can’t accept Kotomine’s story
findings.evidenceJa: 実感が持てなかった
findings.governingReading: Kotomine’s account did not feel real to him
findings.explanation: Shirou’s inability to feel the revelation as real becomes a conscious rejection of it.

findings.highlight: he would kill the sacrifice himself without a second thought
findings.evidenceJa: 速やかに自らの手で事を成した
findings.governingReading: he promptly carried out the deed with his own hands
findings.explanation: Speed and personal execution become absence of reflection.

findings.highlight: A contradictory ideal
findings.evidenceJa: 破綻した理想
findings.governingReading: a broken, self-defeating ideal
findings.explanation: The ideal’s failure is weakened to internal contradiction.

findings.highlight: we were not of the same kind
findings.evidenceJa: 致命的に同朋ではなかった
findings.governingReading: fatally, we were not comrades
findings.explanation: The decisive failure of kinship between Kotomine and Kiritsugu becomes generic difference.

findings.highlight: He pursued his ideal until the moment he destroyed the Holy Grail.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を破壊するまで守られた
findings.governingReading: he preserved that ideal until he destroyed the Grail
findings.explanation: Continuing fidelity to the ideal becomes merely continuing pursuit.

findings.highlight: The reason he was never woundedwas he was wounded from the start.
findings.evidenceJa: それ故にヤツは一つも傷を負わず、そしてアレには、初めから傷しかなかった
findings.governingReading: therefore he received not one wound, and yet from the beginning there was nothing in him but wounds
findings.explanation: A juxtaposed paradox becomes a false causal explanation and loses the distinction between no wounds and nothing but wounds.

findings.highlight: woundedwas he
findings.evidenceJa: 傷を負わず、そして
findings.governingReading: wounded, and yet he
findings.explanation: Missing spacing fuses the predicate.

findings.highlight: an artificial brute
findings.evidenceJa: 作為的な人でなし
findings.governingReading: a deliberately constructed inhuman man
findings.explanation: A chosen absence of humanity becomes generic brutishness.

findings.highlight: you are more similar to him than I
findings.evidenceJa: おまえこそ切嗣に似た部分がある
findings.governingReading: you yourself have aspects resembling Kiritsugu
findings.explanation: The English invents a comparative claim that Shirou resembles Kiritsugu more than Kotomine does.

findings.highlight: Believing in simplicity
findings.evidenceJa: 綺麗事を信じ
findings.governingReading: believing in beautiful but impractical ideals
findings.explanation: Shirou and Kiritsugu’s moral idealism becomes belief in simplicity.

findings.highlight: shouldering the role of a criminal
findings.evidenceJa: 汚れ役を引き受ける
findings.governingReading: taking on the dirty role themselves
findings.explanation: A morally compromising function becomes the specific legal identity of a criminal.

findings.highlight: Turning yourselves into the greatest evil
findings.evidenceJa: 自らを強大な悪として
findings.governingReading: making yourselves into a mighty evil
findings.explanation: Magnitude becomes an unsupported absolute ranking.

findings.highlight: you cannot decide whether to be happy or sad
findings.evidenceJa: 喜ぶべきか悲しむべきか、複雑すぎて心が定まらん
findings.governingReading: I cannot settle whether I should rejoice or grieve
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s professed emotional uncertainty is assigned to Shirou.

findings.highlight: An example of this would be a sacrifice.
findings.evidenceJa: 端的に言えば人柱や生贄
findings.governingReading: plainly, human pillars and sacrificial victims are examples
findings.explanation: One of the two concrete antihero examples disappears and the plural category narrows to one instance.

findings.highlight: getting a high promotion for dying in combat
findings.evidenceJa: 戦死したら恩赦で階級があがる
findings.governingReading: receiving a pardon and a promotion in rank after dying in battle
findings.explanation: The pardon that makes Shirou’s analogy work disappears, while “high promotion” is unnatural.

findings.highlight: Heroes who died as evil
findings.evidenceJa: 悪として葬られた英雄
findings.governingReading: heroes buried or condemned as evil
findings.explanation: Social condemnation is changed into an unclear manner of death.

findings.highlight: They are created by the people, but are not a part of humanity.
findings.evidenceJa: 人が生み出したモノでありながら、決して人の手が混ざらず成長するモノ
findings.governingReading: something created by humans yet growing without human hands ever entering into it
findings.explanation: A paradox about human creation and untouched growth becomes an ontological exclusion from humanity.

findings.highlight: They are an ideal that humans have created
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の生み出した一つの終末
findings.governingReading: one apocalypse created by humanity
findings.explanation: A human-made end of the world becomes an ideal.

findings.highlight: sacrifices to deny the original sin
findings.evidenceJa: 原罪を否定する為の生贄
findings.governingReading: a sacrifice used to deny original sin
findings.explanation: The defined singular antihero mechanism becomes generic plural sacrifices.

findings.highlight: Then you will be a great anti-hero.
findings.evidenceJa: 立派な反英雄という事だ
findings.governingReading: that makes you a fine antihero already
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s present classification of Shirou becomes a future result.

findings.highlight: superhero
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方
findings.governingReading: ally of justice
findings.explanation: The route’s central ideal is again replaced by a genre label.

findings.highlight: powers beyond my position
findings.evidenceJa: 分不相応の力
findings.governingReading: power beyond one’s station or deserts
findings.explanation: The English copies the source relation into an unnatural phrase.

findings.highlight: hard-headed
findings.evidenceJa: 筋金が入っている
findings.governingReading: incorrigible through and through
findings.explanation: Kotomine identifies a deeply ingrained shared nature, not mere stubbornness.

findings.highlight: his smile is friendly
findings.evidenceJa: 慇懃に笑った
findings.governingReading: he smiles with exaggerated formal politeness
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s pointedly courteous irony becomes friendliness.

findings.highlight: Our wishes, our questions, are different
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツの疑問と私の疑問は、それこそ種別が違う
findings.governingReading: His questions and mine are different in kind
findings.explanation: The English adds wishes and blurs Kotomine’s claim about fundamentally different kinds of questions.

findings.highlight: A question by the one who does not have it shall not be answered by the one who does
findings.evidenceJa: 持たざる者の疑問など、もとより持ち得る者の中にはあるまい
findings.governingReading: the question of one who lacks it cannot exist in one capable of possessing it
findings.explanation: An ontological absence inside the possessor becomes a failure to answer someone else’s question.

findings.highlight: that is why they would never have been able to get along
findings.evidenceJa: 故に絶対に相容れない
findings.governingReading: therefore they are absolutely incompatible
findings.explanation: Absolute incompatibility is reduced to the social idea that the two would not get along.

findings.highlight: He had to reject the extra parts
findings.evidenceJa: 余分は処分するしかない
findings.governingReading: there is no choice but to dispose of the excess
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s lethal exclusion logic is softened into rejection.

findings.highlight: ‘something that does not exist’ like the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯という“あり得ないもの”
findings.governingReading: the impossible thing called the Holy Grail
findings.explanation: The Grail is the impossible thing in the source; the English makes it merely an example of one.

findings.highlight: an impossible sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 叶う筈のない魔法
findings.governingReading: Magic that could never be realized
findings.explanation: The work’s marked category Magic is changed to sorcery.

findings.highlight: the more he matured
findings.evidenceJa: 成長すればするほど
findings.governingReading: the more he grew
findings.explanation: Growth under mounting experience becomes psychological maturation.

findings.highlight: attained the miracle-granting Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯に行き着いた
findings.governingReading: ultimately arrived at the Holy Grail as his only path
findings.explanation: Reaching the Grail as the endpoint of Kiritsugu’s reasoning becomes already obtaining it.

findings.highlight: your wish is unattainable by normal means
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の手ではその願いは叶わない
findings.governingReading: the wish cannot be fulfilled by one’s own hands
findings.explanation: Personal inability is generalized into the inadequacy of ordinary methods.

findings.highlight: strayed far away from his ideal
findings.evidenceJa: 自らが自らの理想とかけ離れた人間になった
findings.governingReading: he became a person far removed from his own ideal
findings.explanation: A tragic change in what Kiritsugu became is recast as voluntarily straying from a path.

findings.highlight: For his ideal, and for everything he sacrificed
findings.evidenceJa: 多くのモノを犠牲にして、夢見続けた物の為に
findings.governingReading: for what he continued to dream of while sacrificing many things
findings.explanation: The sacrifices become what Kiritsugu acted for rather than the cost paid for the object of his dream.

findings.highlight: It was his own self that betrayed him
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツ自身が、最後に自分自身を裏切った
findings.governingReading: he himself ultimately betrayed his own self
findings.explanation: The agent and object of Kiritsugu’s self-betrayal are reversed.

findings.highlight: In that instant, I began to feel anger
findings.evidenceJa: まさしくあの瞬間だったろう
findings.governingReading: it was precisely at that moment that I felt fury
findings.explanation: The English invents the onset of Kotomine’s anger rather than identifying its decisive moment.

findings.highlight: the ‘peace’ that humans wish for
findings.evidenceJa: 一人の人間が望んだ“平穏”
findings.governingReading: the peace desired by a single human being
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s interest in the concrete shape of one man’s wish is generalized to humanity’s wish.

findings.highlight: a world without conflict
findings.evidenceJa: 苦しみのない世界
findings.governingReading: a world without conflict and without suffering
findings.explanation: Half of the universally desired peace is omitted.

findings.highlight: An ideal world is one that is the most comfortable
findings.evidenceJa: 願いとは即ち、その人間がもっとも心地よいと感じる在り方
findings.governingReading: a wish is the mode of being that the person finds most comfortable
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s general definition of desire becomes a claim specifically about ideal worlds.

findings.highlight: It does not matter, let it be believing in people or having people believe in me
findings.evidenceJa: 人を信じる事も、人に信じられる事も、どうという事はない
findings.governingReading: whether trusting people or being trusted, neither means anything to me
findings.explanation: The paired trust relations are rendered in malformed English.

findings.highlight: It’s almost like a monologue
findings.evidenceJa: ここにはいない誰かに宛てたような
findings.governingReading: as though addressed to someone who is not here
findings.explanation: The absent imagined addressee disappears, weakening the scene’s controlled hint about Kotomine’s interior life.

findings.highlight: Uhno, hold on
findings.evidenceJa: ういや、ちょっと待った
findings.governingReading: No—wait a second
findings.explanation: The interjection is fused into a nonexistent English word.

findings.highlight: he’ll laugh and make fun of me
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌味と皮肉と嘲笑で返される
findings.governingReading: he would answer with nastiness, irony, and derisive laughter
findings.explanation: Three distinct anticipated modes of Kotomine’s response collapse into generic mockery.

findings.highlight: Didn’t I come to this church because I wanted this question answered?
findings.evidenceJa: マスターとしての立ち振る舞いではなく、ある疑問を晴らす為に、来たくもない教会を訪れた
findings.governingReading: I came to this church, though I wanted no part of it, to resolve a particular doubt rather than learn how a Master should behave
findings.explanation: The English drops Shirou’s aversion to the church and the contrast that recovers his actual purpose.

findings.highlight: they would want to kill you
findings.evidenceJa: おまえは抹殺対象だ
findings.governingReading: you are a designated target for elimination
findings.explanation: A categorical Einzbern status is reduced to a presumed desire.

findings.highlight: who is this Einzbern?
findings.evidenceJa: アインツベルンってなんなんだ
findings.governingReading: what are the Einzberns?
findings.explanation: Shirou’s question about a family is made a question about one person.

findings.highlight: a ritualist
findings.evidenceJa: それを仕組んだ者
findings.governingReading: someone who devised and arranged it
findings.explanation: The architect of the ritual becomes a ritual practitioner.

findings.highlight: to create the Holy Grail’s activation circle
findings.evidenceJa: この地の深くに作り上げた
findings.governingReading: built the Grail-activation formation deep within this land
findings.explanation: The subterranean location of the foundational formation is omitted.

findings.highlight: the Command Spell
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪
findings.governingReading: the Command Spells
findings.explanation: The system of Command Spells is reduced to a singular spell.

findings.highlight: the Command Spell which abuses the heroic spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊を酷使する令呪
findings.governingReading: Command Spells devised to drive Heroic Spirits relentlessly
findings.explanation: A functional coercive mechanism becomes a generic moral accusation of abuse.

findings.highlight: lineage and history far surpassing ours
findings.evidenceJa: 太刀打ちできぬ歴史と血筋
findings.governingReading: history and bloodlines against which neither you nor I could contend
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s categorical inability to contend with the founders is weakened to comparative superiority.

findings.highlight: fatherly master
findings.evidenceJa: 大師父
findings.governingReading: great grandmaster
findings.explanation: A lineage title is mistranslated into a nonsensical paternal description.

findings.highlight: that Schweinorg
findings.evidenceJa: かの時の翁
findings.governingReading: the old man of that time
findings.explanation: The English inserts the proper name Schweinorg where the visible source uses an oblique title.

findings.highlight: lasted for a thousand years without spawning any branch families
findings.evidenceJa: 他と交わらずに一千の年月を重ねた
findings.governingReading: passed a thousand years without branch families or mixing with others
findings.explanation: The Einzberns’ refusal to mix their line with outsiders is omitted.

findings.highlight: barbarism such as mass murder
findings.evidenceJa: 殺して殺して殺し尽くすなどという異次元の蛮行
findings.governingReading: otherworldly barbarity such as killing and killing until everyone was dead
findings.explanation: The source’s relentless accumulation and judgment of the medieval violence are flattened.

findings.highlight: They are crazy
findings.evidenceJa: 人の領域など逸脱した狂気の沙汰
findings.governingReading: madness extending beyond the human domain
findings.explanation: A precise claim about the transhuman scale of a millennium-long project becomes a generic insult.

findings.highlight: not fanatics, not obstinate, nor crazy
findings.evidenceJa: 熱狂的ではなく偏執的ではなく狂信的でもなく
findings.governingReading: neither fervent, obsessive, nor fanatical
findings.explanation: The three denied forms of commitment are mistranslated and partially duplicated.

findings.highlight: to enforce the meaninglessness
findings.evidenceJa: “無意味”さを貫き通してきた
findings.governingReading: carried that meaninglessness through to the end
findings.explanation: An endurance claim becomes malformed English about enforcing an abstraction.

findings.highlight: Normally such people die off after a few decades
findings.evidenceJa: 十年単位ですら忘却され消耗する集団の意思
findings.governingReading: a collective will ordinarily forgotten and exhausted within mere decades
findings.explanation: The erosion of collective purpose becomes the biological death of individual people.

findings.highlight: never straying from their path, always attempting to achieve a common goal
findings.evidenceJa: その何倍も繰り返したあげくただの一度も道を誤らなかった
findings.governingReading: repeated that span many times without once straying from the path
findings.explanation: The extraordinary repetition and absolute absence of deviation are diluted.

findings.highlight: Andit
findings.evidenceJa: そしてやはり
findings.governingReading: And it
findings.explanation: Two English words are fused.

findings.highlight: literally killed their emotions
findings.evidenceJa: 自らを殺す気概で
findings.governingReading: with the resolve to kill themselves
findings.explanation: Self-annihilating resolve becomes emotional suppression.

findings.highlight: cooperate with Makiri and Tohsaka
findings.evidenceJa: 下賎の者たちと協力した
findings.governingReading: cooperate with those they considered lowborn
findings.explanation: The Einzberns’ contemptuous social framing is replaced by names absent from the clause.

findings.highlight: contaminating their own bloodline
findings.evidenceJa: 守り通した血の結束を破って
findings.governingReading: breaking the unity of blood they had preserved
findings.explanation: A breach of protected solidarity becomes the narrator’s unsupported claim of contamination.

findings.highlight: have some sort of burden
findings.evidenceJa: 業を背負っている
findings.governingReading: bear some form of karma
findings.explanation: The Masters’ morally and causally charged karma is generalized to a burden.

findings.highlight: If anyone has the right to own the Holy Grail, it would be one of them
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯はどちらかの手に渡らねば救われぬ
findings.governingReading: the Grail must pass into one family’s hands or they cannot be saved
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s claim of necessity and salvation disappears.

findings.highlight: you do not need to condemn him
findings.evidenceJa: それを非道となじる事はない
findings.governingReading: I will not denounce that as inhuman
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s own judgment becomes advice instructing Shirou how to judge Kiritsugu.

findings.highlight: he held to his belief
findings.evidenceJa: 己が願いの成就に懸けた
findings.governingReading: he staked everything on fulfilling his own wish
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s wager on achieving a wish becomes passive fidelity to a belief.

findings.highlight: everything
findings.evidenceJa: 自身の裡に沈むあらゆる物
findings.governingReading: everything buried within himself
findings.explanation: The inward things Kiritsugu discarded are generalized beyond recognition.

findings.highlight: People who accepted him
findings.evidenceJa: 自分を迎え入れた者たち
findings.governingReading: those who had welcomed him in
findings.explanation: The Einzberns’ concrete act of receiving Kiritsugu becomes abstract acceptance.

findings.highlight: I have to follow my beliefs
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の信じる道を行かなくては
findings.governingReading: I must walk the path I believe in
findings.explanation: Shirou’s commitment to conduct and direction becomes possession of beliefs.

findings.highlight: Are you scared
findings.evidenceJa: 戦意が削がれたのかね
findings.governingReading: has your will to fight been diminished
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s provocation about lost fighting spirit becomes an assertion of fear.

findings.highlight: I raise my head in determination
findings.evidenceJa: それだけだ、と顔をあげる
findings.governingReading: With that, I raise my head
findings.explanation: The English explicitly supplies determination where the source lets the physical gesture carry the resolve.

findings.highlight: nods
findings.evidenceJa: 大仰に頷いた
findings.governingReading: nods grandly and theatrically
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s exaggerated manner disappears.

findings.highlight: Risk your life like Kiritsugu and lure your enemies in
findings.evidenceJa: 夜毎己が命を秤にかけて標的を誘き寄せろ
findings.governingReading: night after night, put your own life on the scales and lure in the target, as Kiritsugu did
findings.explanation: The nightly repetition, weighing metaphor, and singular target vanish from Kotomine’s lethal advice.

findings.highlight: healing magic
findings.evidenceJa: 治癒の魔術
findings.governingReading: healing Magecraft
findings.explanation: The work’s technical category Magecraft is generalized to magic.

findings.highlight: I can handle all the treatments unless they are beyond help
findings.evidenceJa: 間に合うのなら、こちらで治療は引き受けよう
findings.governingReading: if they are brought in time, I will undertake their treatment here
findings.explanation: A condition about reaching Kotomine in time becomes a judgment that the wounds are not beyond help.

findings.highlight: I stop
findings.evidenceJa: 出口に向かっていた足が止まる
findings.governingReading: the feet that had been carrying me toward the exit stop dead
findings.explanation: The physical direction and abruptness of Shirou’s involuntary reaction disappear.

findings.highlight: healing magic
findings.evidenceJa: 治療魔術
findings.governingReading: healing Magecraft
findings.explanation: The work’s technical category Magecraft is again generalized to magic.

findings.highlight: someone die in front of me
findings.evidenceJa: 死病つきに死なれて
findings.governingReading: someone afflicted with a fatal illness died before my eyes
findings.explanation: The fatal illness that motivates Kotomine’s acquisition of healing Magecraft is omitted.

findings.highlight: this time I really do leave
findings.evidenceJa: 外に向かって突き進んだ
findings.governingReading: I thrust ahead toward the outside
findings.explanation: Shirou’s forceful, irritated exit becomes a neutral departure.
